title: KV eviction serialization glitch and tenant upload failover
creator: Alice Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers experienced spikes of 5xx errors and client-observed timeouts during large dataset uploads to Dedicated pools. Root cause analysis shows a race between KV cache compaction/eviction and request streaming serialization in the proxy/runtime boundary. Eviction notifications could race with in-flight request deserialization, leaving a partially-initialized KV fingerprinter and causing proto-deserialize failures in ~0.3% of requests. Those failures surfaced as 5xx from the serving runtime; client SDK retries plus immediate fanout caused amplification and tenant-visible outage windows.

Goals: (1) Fix the race and eliminate the serialization corruption class that leads to 5xx; (2) Add protective mitigations to prevent retry amplification during high-throughput tenant uploads; (3) Roll out a safe remediation with staged canaries and clear rollback paths; (4) Produce runbook snippets and postmortem notes for customers.

Proposed fix (hotpatch + planned follow-up):
- Hotpatch: make eviction notification handler idempotent and pre-validate KV fingerprint structures before they are used for request deserialization. Add defensive checks that convert recoverable deserialize errors into 429/short-circuit fast-fail with a short Retry-After header instead of 5xx.
- Retry policy change: for upload-related routes, temporarily switch to jittered exponential backoff and add tenant-scoped in-flight request caps to avoid fanout amplification.
- Safe rollout: canary 5% of Dedicated pools -> 25% -> 100% over 6 hours with automated health gates (error-rate, p95 latency, KV compaction rate).
- Post-fix hardening: add a per-tenant upload coordinator that coordinates KV compactions with long-lived upload streams, and add a lightweight per-request version token so deserializers can reject stale/partial fingerprints early with deterministic fast-fail.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hotpatch deployed to hosted and dedicated-proxy fleet with no increase in p99 latency > 10ms above baseline.
- Error rate for affected routes reduced to background levels within the canary window and sustained for 24 hours after rollout.
- No customer has recurring escalations from the same root cause after the full rollout.
- Playbook updated: incident runbook section added and linked in comments; clear rollback command documented.

Monitoring and observability:
- Datadog dashboard: dd://dash/hosted/kv-eviction-serialization (incident graph added, source: APM + runtime metrics).
- Alerts: temporarily raise threshold for the route-specific alarm to avoid noisy paging during rollout; create a secondary alert that fires if 5xx > 0.5% for 10m.

Rollback plan:
- Revert hotpatch via canary control to previous runtime image; automatically disable upload-specific retry policy TTL to restore original behaviour.
- If revert is insufficient, proactively quarantine impacted tenants to Dedicated fallback circuits and coordinate customer comms.

Security review required: "true"
